analysis: What changed versus the 8:00 AM brief: the bounce held into midday but stopped broadening — the S&P 500 is +1.02% at 7,428.63 and the Nasdaq +1.80% at 24,751.94 (11:35 AM ET), and the Dow has clawed all the way back to +0.09% after opening down 474 points. The tell is under the surface: more S&P 500 names declined than advanced per AP, so the index gains are still carried by chips and megacaps, not a broad rally. Nvidia is the microcosm — +3.87% to ~$188.63 but well off its $194.90 session high, and the fresh Bloomberg report that new Southeast Asia Cloud Partners must enroll in Nvidia's Fleet Intelligence amid a US probe into chip diversion to China adds a new overhang on the same name. QQQ cleared the 658 line WSB was watching ($661.24, +2.19%), which the crowd will read as a small win for the V-shape camp — but Thursday's tape says retail dumped stocks at one of the highest rates since the COVID crash (net outflows $257M), so Friday's buyers are stepping in against real capitulation, not just a quiet tape. The new tension is rates: the hot payrolls print (+165K vs 59K expected) revived rate-hike chatter even as Michigan sentiment beat, and yields are climbing again after Thursday's flight to safety. Signal vs noise: the Dow's full recovery and QQQ holding above 658 are signal; the Lam Research $25B buyback (+~9-12%) is a real semis-specific catalyst, while the chip-tracking probe and Anthropic's repricing are the live structural overhangs. The afternoon test is whether the bounce survives the close with vol-control selling still queued and Iran weekend risk in the background.

headlines.headline: The bounce held into midday: as of 11:35 a.m. ET the S&P 500 was up 1.02% at 7,428.63 and the Nasdaq Composite up 1.80% at 24,751.94, while the Dow recovered all the way to +0.09% at 51,569.69 after opening down 474 points.
headlines.why_it_matters: The Dow's full round-trip from -474 at the open to flat-to-green shows dip-buying spread beyond chips — but the gains are still narrow, with more S&P 500 names declining than advancing per AP.

headlines.headline: Nvidia cooled from +7.05% at the open to +3.87% at about $188.63 by 11:42 a.m. ET (prior close $181.60), off its $194.90 session high; the stock is down about 15% since Oct. 6 and reports Q3 earnings Nov. 17.
headlines.why_it_matters: The chip bounce is real but fading from its best levels for a second straight reading — early buyers are taking profits, and Nov. 17 earnings are the next real test of the AI demand story.

headlines.headline: Nvidia is tightening oversight of AI accelerators sold in Southeast Asia: Bloomberg reported Friday that new Nvidia Cloud Partners in the region must enroll in Nvidia's Fleet Intelligence system as US authorities examine suspected diversion of restricted chips to China.
headlines.why_it_matters: A fresh regulatory overhang lands on the same name leading the bounce — tighter chip tracking feeds the demand-restriction worry that drove Thursday's rout.

headlines.headline: Megacaps at midday: Tesla +5.10% to $361.24, Meta +2.77% to $621.86, Alphabet +1.67% to $287.30 and Amazon +1.09% to $263.06, while Apple (+0.03% to $344.28) and Microsoft (+0.07% to $536.28) are essentially flat.
headlines.why_it_matters: The recovery is led by the names hit hardest Thursday — Tesla and Meta — while Apple and Microsoft sit out, so the megacap split from the open is still in place.

headlines.headline: Lam Research jumped 8.8-12% after announcing a share repurchase program worth up to $25 billion plus a quarterly dividend of $0.33 per share, the strongest single-stock catalyst in the semiconductor bounce.
headlines.why_it_matters: A $25B buyback is a real capital-return signal in the middle of the AI-capex debate — it gives the chip bounce a company-specific leg beyond dip-buying.

headlines.headline: Moderna rose nearly 4% after third-quarter results came in well above expectations, one of the few earnings-driven gainers on a tape still dominated by Thursday's rout.
headlines.why_it_matters: An earnings beat is still being paid — the contrast with Thursday's guidance-cut punishments (DraftKings -28%) shows the market is discriminating on results, not just selling everything.

headlines.headline: Retail investors dumped stocks on Thursday at one of the highest rates since the COVID crash, with net outflows reaching $257 million, even as some younger investors and advisers bought QQQ into the selloff; the mood on r/wallstreetbets was split between buying calls for a swift rebound and calling Thursday 'just the appetizer.'
headlines.why_it_matters: Friday's bounce is happening against genuine retail capitulation, not a quiet tape — the dip-buying has to absorb real selling, which is why the rally stays narrow and fragile.

usac.why_it_matters: USAC +3.09% to $24.99 at midday; no fresh company news. The $0.525 per-unit distribution pays TODAY, Friday Nov 6, to holders of record Oct 26. The Nov 3 Q3 story carries forward: record revenue $357.2M (+43% year over year, vs ~$348.32M consensus), record Adjusted EBITDA $197.3M, DCF coverage 1.67x, EPS $0.33 vs $0.3345 expected, distribution held at $0.525, full-year guidance tightened to Adjusted EBITDA $770-780M and DCF $495-505M. On the call, management said over 60% of 2027 horsepower deliveries are contracted (about 90% of first-half deliveries), but flagged cost pressure: monthly lubricant costs exited Q3 about 25% above first-half levels and diesel hit an all-time high in September, with pricing not yet fully reflecting the increases.
